finding.claim: The /preview route fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no validation, so an unauthenticated caller can make the server request internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), localhost services or any other address. The response status and the first 500 characters of the body are returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (query parameter 'url' on GET /preview)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, which follows redirects by default; the result is returned at app.py:17

trace.note: @app.route('/preview') registers the handler with no authentication decorator
target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled value
requests.get(target) is called directly on that value
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned in the JSON response

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no host allowlist, no private/loopback IP check, no authentication, and no redirect restriction on this route. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:24 exists only in /partner and is not applied here, so this is the sibling handler that lacks the check. The only limits are timeout=5 and the 500-character body truncation, neither of which prevents access.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the `url` query parameter and passes it straight to requests.get at app.py:16 with no auth, scheme, host or IP check (the ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:24 is only in /partner), and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 characters of the body.
